snippet.title: 9 Unsexy Habits That Will Put You Ahead of 99% of People
snippet.description:
Subscribe to my newsletter → https://www.sandeepswadia.com/newsletter 

Most people think big goals create big results.
Ironically, research suggests the opposite.

After studying people for over 20 years, New York University researchers found that vividly imagining success can actually make you less likely to achieve it. Why? Because your brain gets rewarded for the fantasy before you've done the work.

In this episode, I break down why meaningful change rarely comes from motivation, vision boards, or ambitious goals—and why it almost always comes from small, boring habits that quietly reshape your attention, energy, and happiness.

You'll learn how to:

• Break overwhelming goals into tiny actions that actually get done
• Recover quickly when you fall into bad habits instead of spiraling
• Eliminate mental clutter and regain control of your attention
• Use writing as a tool for clearer thinking and better decisions
• Work with your brain's natural energy cycles instead of fighting them
• Improve sleep quality by understanding how caffeine really affects you
• Build habits that survive bad days, low motivation, and setbacks
• Create more gratitude, perspective, and resilience in everyday life
• Develop systems that continue working long after motivation disappears

I also share lessons from a Mount Everest climber, insights from neuroscience, sleep research, quantum physics, Amazon's decision-making culture, and practical ideas from thinkers like James Clear, Andrew Huberman, Jeff Bezos, and Max Planck.

Most importantly, you'll learn why lasting transformation is rarely about becoming a different person.

It's about becoming the kind of person who consistently takes the next step.

Because success is not built on extraordinary moments.

It's built on ordinary actions repeated long enough to become who you are.

snippet.title: 5 Things To Do Instead Of Wasting Your Evenings
snippet.description:
Subscribe to my newsletter → https://www.sandeepswadia.com/newsletter 

Most people think they don't have enough time.

Ironically, the average full-time worker gets nearly 1,500 hours of free time every year—the equivalent of almost 36 extra work weeks hiding inside their evenings and weekends.

In this episode, I break down why the quality of your life is often determined by what happens after work. Because your evenings don't just end the day—they shape the future you wake up to.

You'll learn how to:

• Audit your evenings using the "Evening Bank Account" framework
• Distinguish between activities that create energy and those that drain it
• Stop confusing relaxation with genuine recovery
• Use the 3C Framework (Clock, Compass, Climate) to make better decisions with your time
• Align your evenings with your natural biological rhythms
• Invest in the three areas that matter most: body, bonds, and future bets
• Adapt your routines during both peacetime and wartime seasons of life
• Build an "Enough Evening" that works even when life gets chaotic
• Eliminate unnecessary decisions that consume mental energy
• Use reflection and sleep to create better days tomorrow

I also share lessons from my early career, insights from psychology and sleep research, and stories involving leaders like Barack Obama, Steve Jobs, Anna Wintour, Sam Altman, and Neil deGrasse Tyson.

Most importantly, you'll learn that extraordinary lives are rarely built during extraordinary moments.

They're built during ordinary evenings.

Because if you live to be 80, you'll have roughly 22,000 of them.

And what you do with those evenings ultimately becomes your life.
